summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia s/p double cord transplant, chronic GVHD, and COP, was admitted with fever, hypotension, cough, and weakness. He was found to have left lower lobe pneumonia on chest X-ray and was treated with IV vancomycin and ceftazidime in the ICU before transitioning to oral levofloxacin. Hypotension was managed with IV fluids and stress-dose hydrocortisone, later switched back to home prednisone. Acute kidney injury, likely pre-renal, resolved with rehydration. He developed antibiotic-associated diarrhea on hospital day 5, treated empirically with metronidazole despite negative C. diff toxin tests; symptoms improved. He remained afebrile, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home on day 7 with instructions to complete antibiotic courses and follow up with oncology. C. diff PCR remained pending at discharge.
problems: Acute myeloid leukemia, without mention of having achieved remission
Other dependence on machines, supplemental oxygen
